title: Derived enriched Yoneda and coherent representability
statement:
Fix universes large enough that the object sets and mapping complexes below are small [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a differential graded category over $\mathbf Z$: its objects form a set, each $\mathcal A(X,Y)$ is a cochain complex of abelian groups, and composition is an associative unital chain map $\mathcal A(Y,Z)\otimes\mathcal A(X,Y)\to\mathcal A(X,Z)$. A cochain complex has maps $d^i:K^i\to K^{i+1}$ with $d^{i+1}d^i=0$; quasi-isomorphisms induce isomorphisms on all cohomology groups. A right dg module is a dg functor $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$, equivalently complexes $P(X)$ with unital associative composition actions $P(Y)\otimes\mathcal A(X,Y)\to P(X)$. Let $\mathbf{Mod}(\mathcal A)$ be their enhanced localization at objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, retaining derived mapping complexes and homotopy coherent compositions. It may be modeled by homotopically projective dg modules, meaning modules $P$ for which the complex of module maps from $P$ to any objectwise acyclic module is acyclic. Write $h_X=\mathcal A(-,X)$.

Derived evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_X$ is an equivalence of mapping complexes
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Mod}(\mathcal A)}(h_X,P)\simeq P(X),$$
natural in $X$ and $P$. Consequently $X\mapsto h_X$ is fully faithful on derived mapping complexes and identifies $\mathcal A$, up to enhanced equivalence, with the full enhanced subcategory of modules equivalent to some $h_X$. Here $\mathcal A$ is regarded up to quasi-equivalence, a dg functor inducing quasi-isomorphisms on mapping complexes and an essentially surjective functor on the category with morphisms $H^0\mathcal A(X,Y)$. Form diagram and transformation objects using derived dg functor categories: their functors are allowed after replacing dg categories by quasi-equivalent dg models, and their transformation objects retain all homotopy coherent natural transformations. In particular any homotopy coherent diagram in $\mathbf{Mod}(\mathcal A)$ whose objects belong to this full subcategory factors coherently through this Yoneda embedding; the space of factorizations together with the specified comparison to the original diagram is contractible. This applies to coherent transformations and their higher homotopies between such diagrams, preserving composition and identities. It applies only to diagrams already given in the enhanced module category, not to diagrams specified merely on ordinary homotopy categories.

proof.text:
Work with right actions, so a homogeneous module map $f$ satisfies $f(ma)=f(m)a$, without a sign. Its differential is $df=d_Pf-(-1)^{|f|}f d_{h_X}$. On the ordinary complex of dg-module maps define
$$e_{X,P}(f)=f_X(1_X),\qquad (s_{X,P}(p))_Y(a)=pa\quad(a\in\mathcal A(Y,X)).$$
For $a:Z\to Y$ and $b:Y\to X$, associativity gives $(pb)a=p(ba)$, so $s(p)$ is a graded right-module map. The unit gives $e(s(p))=p$, while right-linearity gives $s(e(f))_Y(a)=f_X(1_X)a=f_Y(a)$. Since $d(1_X)=0$, $e(df)=d_P(e(f))$. Conversely, for $|p|=r$, the Leibniz identity gives
$$d_P(pa)-(-1)^rp\,d_{\mathcal A}(a)=(d_Pp)a,$$
so $d(s(p))=s(d_Pp)$. Thus $e$ and $s$ are mutually inverse chain maps. Module maps commute with the right action, so these formulas are natural in $P$. Precomposing with the map $h_{X'}\to h_X$ determined by a closed degree-zero arrow $a:X'\to X$ sends evaluation $p$ to $pa$, giving naturality in $X$. For a homogeneous arrow $a:X\to Y$ of degree $s$ and $f:h_Y\to P$ of degree $r$, contravariance of the enriched Hom functor sends $f$ to $(-1)^{sr}f\circ h_a$, where $(h_a)_Z(c)=ac$. Evaluation gives $e_{X,P}((-1)^{sr}f\circ h_a)=(-1)^{sr}f_X(a)=(-1)^{sr}f_Y(1_Y)a$. The dg functor associated to the right action has $P(a)(p)=(-1)^{s|p|}pa$, so this is exactly $P(a)(e_{Y,P}(f))$. For a homogeneous module map $g:P\to P\prime$, evaluation gives $e_{X,P\prime}(g\circ f)=g_X(e_{X,P}(f))$. These equations prove dg naturality in both variables with the signs explicit. No statement about derived modules is assumed in this calculation.

proof.text:
If $N$ is objectwise acyclic, step 1 identifies $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal A}(h_X,N)$ with the acyclic complex $N(X)$. Hence $h_X$ is homotopically projective by the definition in the statement. Apply [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution] with $\mathcal B=\mathcal A$, $Q=h_X$ and arbitrary $M=P$: its computation of derived mapping complexes identifies $R\operatorname{Hom}(h_X,P)$ with $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal A}(h_X,P)$. Composing with $e_{X,P}$ is the asserted derived evaluation equivalence. More concretely, if $q:QP\to P$ is a homotopically projective replacement from the same node, it is the zigzag
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal A}(h_X,QP)\xrightarrow{\ e\ }QP(X)\xrightarrow{q(X)}P(X).$$
The first arrow is an isomorphism and the second a quasi-isomorphism. Step 1 is natural before localization; evaluation preserves objectwise quasi-isomorphisms by definition. The compatibility with localization in the cited node therefore gives naturality in the enhanced variables $X$ and $P$, independently of the chosen replacements. This also justifies the homotopically projective presentation used in the statement.

proof.text:
Set $P=h_Y$ in step 1. It gives an isomorphism of complexes
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal A}(h_X,h_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal A(X,Y).$$
Its inverse sends $a:X\to Y$ to postcomposition by $a$. Composing these maps sends $b\otimes a$ to postcomposition by $ba$, and $1_X$ to $1_{h_X}$, because $b(ac)=(ba)c$ and $1_Xc=c$. Thus $h:X\mapsto h_X$ is a dg functor inducing these isomorphisms on all Hom complexes. By step 2 the same complexes compute the derived maps, proving derived full faithfulness. Let $\mathcal E$ be the full dg subcategory of homotopically projective modules whose images in the localization are equivalent to some $h_X$. The localization presentation in [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution] identifies these equivalences with isomorphisms in $H^0$ of the projective model. Therefore $H^0h:\!H^0\mathcal A\to H^0\mathcal E$ is essentially surjective, while the displayed isomorphism gives the local quasi-isomorphisms. By the definition of quasi-equivalence, $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal E$ is a quasi-equivalence. This identifies $\mathcal A$ with the asserted full essential image, without choosing a strict inverse dg functor.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph 2: representing-object uniqueness via a quasi-equivalence onto the full essential image; Genovese section 4.2

proof.text:
Let a homotopy coherent diagram $F$ in the enhanced module category be given, indexed by a small dg category $\mathcal J$ in the universes of the statement. Use the projective-module presentation of [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution]. Every vertex of $F$ then belongs to $\mathcal E$ of step 3. Corestriction to this full enhanced subcategory requires no new arrows or homotopies: each component of each simplex of the coherent diagram has its vertices in $\mathcal E$, and the full-subcategory condition retains all such mapping and composition data. For a quasi-functor model this can equally be read after the source replacement permitted by [lem-coef-dg-quasifunctor-invariance]: a representing dg functor into the projective-module category lands in its full dg subcategory $\mathcal E$. The same full-subcategory observation applies to transformations between such diagrams. Apply [lem-coef-dg-quasifunctor-invariance] to the quasi-equivalence $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal E$ proved in step 3. It gives an enhanced equivalence
$$h_*:\mathbf R\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{dg}}(\mathcal J,\mathcal A)\xrightarrow{\simeq}\mathbf R\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{dg}}(\mathcal J,\mathcal E).$$
Essential surjectivity now supplies a lifted diagram $\widetilde F$ and an invertible coherent transformation $h_*\widetilde F\simeq F$. The original diagram, including all its coherences, was input to this equivalence; none has been reconstructed just from an $H^0$ diagram. The use of derived functor categories and of source replacements is essential, since strict dg functor categories need not preserve quasi-equivalences.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph 2: coherent realization using derived internal Hom; Keller sections 4.2-4.3, Theorems 4.1-4.5

proof.text: The space of pairs $(\widetilde F,\theta:h_*\widetilde F\simeq F)$ is the homotopy fiber over $F$ of the equivalence on maximal homotopy groupoids in [lem-coef-dg-quasifunctor-invariance], applied to $h$. For completeness, take an inverse equivalence $v$ with its unit and counit homotopies. A point of this fiber corresponds to an object $G$ and a path $G\simeq vF$; this space contracts to $(vF,1_{vF})$ by the path itself. This is the homotopy fiber of an identity equivalence at $vF$, so the contraction includes paths between choices and all their higher homotopies. Consequently the factorization space with its specified comparison is contractible. The comparison is part of the pair: the space of representing objects alone can have nontrivial automorphisms.

source.place: Agent homotopy-fiber argument following the derived-functor equivalence in proof paragraph 2

proof.text:
For any two lifted diagrams $\widetilde F,\widetilde G$, the same [lem-coef-dg-quasifunctor-invariance] gives the equivalence of transformation complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}(\widetilde F,\widetilde G)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(h_*\widetilde F,h_*\widetilde G).$$
Use the specified comparison transformations of step 4 to identify the right side with transformations of the original diagrams. The inverse equivalence therefore lifts every coherent transformation, and the homotopy fiber over any specified transformation or higher homotopy is contractible by the argument of step 5. Postcomposition by $h$ preserves composition and identities; its inverse as an enhanced equivalence comes with the corresponding coherent comparison homotopies. For example, the two candidates obtained by lifting a composite or by composing the lifts map to the same composite on the right, so that fiber supplies their comparison and all its higher compatibilities. This proves the assertions about transformations and higher homotopies. All arguments concern the supplied enhanced diagrams and do not assert that arbitrary diagrams in an ordinary homotopy category lift.
